sanskrit: yadi cet khādako na syān na tadā ghātako bhavet ghātakaḥ khādakārthāya taṃ ghātayati vai naraḥ
english: If there were no eater, there would be no slayer; it is for the eater's sake that a man has the creature killed.

sanskrit: abhakṣyam etad iti vā iti hiṃsā nivartate khādakārtham ato hiṃsā mṛgādīnāṃ pravartate
english: When one resolves, 'this is not to be eaten,' the killing ceases; it is for the eater's sake that the slaughter of deer and the rest goes forward.

sanskrit: yasmād grasati caivāyur hiṃsakānāṃ mahādyute tasmād vivarjayen māṃsaṃ ya icched bhūtim ātmanaḥ
english: Since it devours the very lifespan of those who do violence, O greatly radiant one, let him who desires his own welfare abstain from flesh.

sanskrit: trātāraṃ nādhigacchanti raudrāḥ prāṇivihiṃsakāḥ udvejanīyā bhūtānāṃ yathā vyālamṛgās tathā
english: The cruel ones who do violence to living beings find no protector; they are dreaded by all creatures, just as beasts of prey are.

sanskrit: lobhād vā buddhimohād vā balavīryārtham eva ca saṃsargād vātha pāpānām adharmarucitā nṛṇām
english: Out of greed, or delusion of mind, or for the sake of strength and vigor, or through the company of the wicked, men come to take delight in unrighteousness.

sanskrit: svamāṃsaṃ paramāṃsena yo vardhayitum icchati udvignavāse vasati yatratatrābhijāyate
english: He who wishes to fatten his own flesh with the flesh of another dwells in a state of perpetual dread, born again wherever such a fate awaits him.

sanskrit: dhanyaṃ yaśasyam āyuṣyaṃ svargyaṃ svastyayanaṃ mahat māṃsasyābhakṣaṇaṃ prāhur niyatāḥ paramarṣayaḥ
english: The disciplined supreme sages declare the abstention from flesh to be auspicious, bringing renown, long life, heaven, and great well-being.

sanskrit: idaṃ tu khalu kaunteya śrutam āsīt purā mayā mārkaṇḍeyasya vadato ye doṣā māṃsabhakṣaṇe
english: Now this, O son of Kuntī, I once heard long ago from the lips of Mārkaṇḍeya as he spoke of the faults that lie in the eating of flesh.

sanskrit: yo hi khādati māṃsāni prāṇināṃ jīvitārthinām hatānāṃ vā mṛtānāṃ vā yathā hantā tathaiva saḥ
english: He who eats the flesh of living creatures that long for life, whether slain or already dead, is just as guilty as the slayer himself.

sanskrit: dhanena krāyako hanti khādakaś copabhogataḥ ghātako vadhabandhābhyām ity eṣa trividho vadhaḥ
english: The buyer kills with his wealth, the eater by his enjoyment, the slayer by killing and binding: thus the killing is threefold.

sanskrit: akhādann anumodaṃś ca bhāvadoṣeṇa mānavaḥ yo 'numanyeta hantavyaṃ so 'pi doṣeṇa lipyate
english: Even the man who does not eat but approves is stained by the fault of his intent; he who consents that a creature should be slain is likewise tainted by the sin.

sanskrit: adhṛṣyaḥ sarvabhūtānām āyuṣmān nīrujaḥ sukhī bhavaty abhakṣayan māṃsaṃ dayāvān prāṇinām iha
english: The man who eats no flesh and is compassionate toward living beings becomes here unassailable by all creatures, long-lived, free of disease, and happy.

sanskrit: hiraṇyadānair godānair bhūmidānaiś ca sarvaśaḥ māṃsasyābhakṣaṇe dharmo viśiṣṭaḥ syād iti śrutiḥ
english: The sacred teaching holds that the merit in abstaining from flesh surpasses in every way the gift of gold, of cattle, and of land.

sanskrit: aprokṣitaṃ vṛthāmāṃsaṃ vidhihīnaṃ na bhakṣayet bhakṣayan nirayaṃ yāti naro nāsty atra saṃśayaḥ
english: Let none eat flesh unconsecrated, taken in vain and outside the ordinance; the man who eats it goes to hell—of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: prokṣitābhyukṣitaṃ māṃsaṃ tathā brāhmaṇakāmyayā alpadoṣam iha jñeyaṃ viparīte tu lipyate
english: Flesh consecrated and sprinkled, or eaten at a brāhmaṇa's wish, is to be known as of slight fault here; but in the contrary case one is defiled.

sanskrit: khādakasya kṛte jantuṃ yo hanyāt puruṣādhamaḥ mahādoṣakaras tatra khādako na tu ghātakaḥ
english: The basest of men who slays a creature for the eater's sake works a great sin there; in such a case it is the eater, not the slayer alone, who bears the guilt.

sanskrit: ijyāyajñaśrutikṛtair yo mārgair abudho janaḥ hanyāj jantuṃ māṃsagṛddhrī sa vai narakabhāṅ naraḥ
english: The witless man, greedy for flesh, who slays a creature under the pretext of sacrifice, ritual, and scripture, is verily one doomed to hell.

sanskrit: bhakṣayitvā tu yo māṃsaṃ paścād api nivartate tasyāpi sumahān dharmo yaḥ pāpād vinivartate
english: Even he who has eaten flesh but afterward turns away from it gains great merit, for he turns back from sin.

sanskrit: āhartā cānumantā ca viśastā krayavikrayī saṃskartā copabhoktā ca ghātakāḥ sarva eva te
english: The fetcher, the consenter, the butcher, the buyer and seller, the cook, and the consumer—all of these are slayers.

sanskrit: idam anyat tu vakṣyāmi pramāṇaṃ vidhinirmitam purāṇam ṛṣibhir juṣṭaṃ vedeṣu pariniścitam
english: But now I shall tell you another authority, established by ordinance, ancient, honored by the sages, and determined in the Vedas.

sanskrit: pravṛttilakṣaṇe dharme phalārthibhir abhidrute yathoktaṃ rājaśārdūla na tu tan mokṣakāṅkṣiṇām
english: This is taught, O tiger among kings, within the dharma marked by ritual action, sought by those who desire its fruits; but it is not for those who long for liberation.

sanskrit: havir yat saṃskṛtaṃ mantraiḥ prokṣitābhyukṣitaṃ śuci vedoktena pramāṇena pitṝṇāṃ prakriyāsu ca ato 'nyathā vṛthāmāṃsam abhakṣyaṃ manur abravīt
english: The oblation hallowed by sacred verses, consecrated and sprinkled and pure, by the authority declared in the Veda and used in the rites for the ancestors—anything otherwise is flesh taken in vain and not to be eaten, so Manu has declared.

sanskrit: asvargyam ayaśasyaṃ ca rakṣovad bharatarṣabha vidhinā hi narāḥ pūrvaṃ māṃsaṃ rājann abhakṣayan
english: Such eating bars heaven and renown and is fit for demons, O bull of the Bharatas; for in former times men ate flesh, O king, only according to the ordinance.

sanskrit: ya icchet puruṣo 'tyantam ātmānaṃ nirupadravam sa varjayeta māṃsāni prāṇinām iha sarvaśaḥ
english: The man who would have himself wholly free from harm should in every way shun the flesh of living beings here.

sanskrit: śrūyate hi purākalpe nṛṇāṃ vrīhimayaḥ paśuḥ yenāyajanta yajvānaḥ puṇyalokaparāyaṇāḥ
english: For we hear that in the ancient age men used a sacrificial victim made of rice, with which the sacrificers, devoted to holy worlds, performed their offerings.

sanskrit: ṛṣibhiḥ saṃśayaṃ pṛṣṭo vasuś cedipatiḥ purā abhakṣyam iti māṃsaṃ sa prāha bhakṣyam iti prabho
english: Long ago, when the sages put to Vasu, lord of the Cedis, the doubt whether flesh was not to be eaten, he declared, O lord, that it was to be eaten.

sanskrit: ākāśān medinīṃ prāptas tataḥ sa pṛthivīpatiḥ etad eva punaś coktvā viveśa dharaṇītalam
english: Fallen from the sky to the earth, that lord of the world, having again spoken these very words, sank into the surface of the ground.

sanskrit: prajānāṃ hitakāmena tv agastyena mahātmanā āraṇyāḥ sarvadaivatyāḥ prokṣitās tapasā mṛgāḥ
english: But the great-souled Agastya, desiring the good of all creatures, by his austerity consecrated the wild deer of the forest as sacred to all the gods.

sanskrit: kriyā hy evaṃ na hīyante pitṛdaivatasaṃśritāḥ prīyante pitaraś caiva nyāyato māṃsatarpitāḥ
english: Thus the rites that pertain to the ancestors and the gods are not abandoned, and the fathers too are pleased when satisfied with flesh in the proper manner.

sanskrit: idaṃ tu śṛṇu rājendra kīrtyamānaṃ mayānagha abhakṣaṇe sarvasukhaṃ māṃsasya manujādhipa
english: But hear this, O lord of kings, as I proclaim it, O sinless one: in the abstention from flesh lies every happiness, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: yas tu varṣaśataṃ pūrṇaṃ tapas tapyet sudāruṇam yaś caikaṃ varjayen māṃsaṃ samam etan mataṃ mama
english: He who should practice the most severe austerity for a full hundred years, and he who should renounce flesh but once—these two I hold to be equal.

sanskrit: kaumude tu viśeṣeṇa śuklapakṣe narādhipa varjayet sarvamāṃsāni dharmo hy atra vidhīyate
english: And especially in the bright fortnight of the month of Kārttika, O ruler of men, let one abstain from all flesh, for therein merit is ordained.

sanskrit: caturo vārṣikān māsān yo māṃsaṃ parivarjayet catvāri bhadrāṇy āpnoti kīrtim āyur yaśo balam
english: He who shuns flesh through the four months of the rainy season obtains the four blessings: renown, long life, fame, and strength.

sanskrit: atha vā māsam apy ekaṃ sarvamāṃsāny abhakṣayan atītya sarvaduḥkhāni sukhī jīven nirāmayaḥ
english: Or even for a single month abstaining from all flesh, having passed beyond every sorrow, he lives happy and free of disease.

sanskrit: ye varjayanti māṃsāni māsaśaḥ pakṣaśo 'pi vā teṣāṃ hiṃsānivṛttānāṃ brahmaloko vidhīyate
english: For those who shun flesh by months, or even by fortnights, who have desisted from violence, the world of Brahmā is ordained.

sanskrit: māṃsaṃ tu kaumudaṃ pakṣaṃ varjitaṃ pārtha rājabhiḥ sarvabhūtātmabhūtais tair vijñātārthaparāvaraiḥ
english: Flesh was shunned during the Kārttika fortnight, O Pārtha, by those kings who looked on all beings as their own self and who knew things high and low.

sanskrit: nābhāgenāmbarīṣeṇa gayena ca mahātmanā āyuṣā cānaraṇyena dilīparaghupūrubhiḥ
english: By Nābhāga, by Ambarīṣa, and by the great-souled Gaya, by Āyus and Anaraṇya, by Dilīpa, Raghu, and Pūru,

sanskrit: kārtavīryāniruddhābhyāṃ nahuṣeṇa yayātinā nṛgeṇa viṣvagaśvena tathaiva śaśabindunā yuvanāśvena ca tathā śibinauśīnareṇa ca
english: by Kārtavīrya and Aniruddha, by Nahuṣa and Yayāti, by Nṛga and Viṣvagaśva, and likewise by Śaśabindu, by Yuvanāśva too, and by Śibi the son of Uśīnara,

sanskrit: śyenacitreṇa rājendra somakena vṛkeṇa ca raivatena rantidevena vasunā sṛñjayena ca
english: by Śyenacitra, O lord of kings, by Somaka and Vṛka, by Raivata, by Rantideva, by Vasu and Sṛñjaya,

sanskrit: duḥṣantena karūṣeṇa rāmālarkanalais tathā virūpāśvena niminā janakena ca dhīmatā
english: by Duḥṣanta, by Karūṣa, by Rāma, Alarka, and Nala, by Virūpāśva, by Nimi, and by the wise Janaka,

sanskrit: silena pṛthunā caiva vīrasenena caiva ha ikṣvākuṇā śaṃbhunā ca śvetena sagareṇa ca
english: by Sila and by Pṛthu, and by Vīrasena too, by Ikṣvāku and Śambhu, by Śveta and Sagara—

sanskrit: etaiś cānyaiś ca rājendra purā māṃsaṃ na bhakṣitam śāradaṃ kaumudaṃ māsaṃ tatas te svargam āpnuvan
english: by these and others, O lord of kings, no flesh was eaten of old during the autumnal month of Kārttika, and thereby they attained heaven.

sanskrit: brahmaloke ca tiṣṭhanti jvalamānāḥ śriyānvitāḥ upāsyamānā gandharvaiḥ strīsahasrasamanvitāḥ
english: And they abide in the world of Brahmā, blazing and endowed with splendor, attended by gandharvas and surrounded by thousands of women.

sanskrit: tad etad uttamaṃ dharmam ahiṃsālakṣaṇaṃ śubham ye caranti mahātmāno nākapṛṣṭhe vasanti te
english: The great-souled ones who practice this supreme and auspicious dharma, marked by non-violence, dwell upon the vault of heaven.

sanskrit: madhu māṃsaṃ ca ye nityaṃ varjayantīha dhārmikāḥ janmaprabhṛti madyaṃ ca sarve te munayaḥ smṛtāḥ viśiṣṭatāṃ jñātiṣu ca labhante nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: The righteous who from birth forever shun honey, flesh, and liquor are all reckoned as sages, and they attain eminence among their kinsmen—of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: āpannaś cāpado mucyed baddho mucyeta bandhanāt mucyet tathāturo rogād duḥkhān mucyeta duḥkhitaḥ
english: One in distress is freed from his distress, the bound is loosed from his bonds, the sick is delivered from disease, and the suffering from his suffering.

sanskrit: tiryagyoniṃ na gaccheta rūpavāṃś ca bhaven naraḥ buddhimān vai kuruśreṣṭha prāpnuyāc ca mahad yaśaḥ
english: Such a man does not pass to the wombs of beasts, but becomes comely and wise, O best of the Kurus, and attains great renown.

sanskrit: etat te kathitaṃ rājan māṃsasya parivarjane pravṛttau ca nivṛttau ca vidhānam ṛṣinirmitam
english: This, O king, has been told to you—the ordinance fashioned by the sages concerning the shunning of flesh, both in its practice and in its renunciation.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ime vai mānavā loke bhṛśaṃ māṃsasya gṛddhinaḥ visṛjya bhakṣān vividhān yathā rakṣogaṇās tathā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: These men in the world are exceedingly greedy for flesh; forsaking the many other foods, they crave it as the hosts of rākṣasas do.

sanskrit: nāpūpān vividhākārāñ śākāni vividhāni ca ṣāḍavān rasayogāṃś ca tathecchanti yathāmiṣam
english: They do not desire cakes of various shapes, nor the many kinds of vegetables, nor the six-flavored relishes and savory dishes, as they desire meat.

sanskrit: tatra me buddhir atraiva visarge parimuhyate na manye rasataḥ kiṃ cin māṃsato 'stīha kiṃ cana
english: Herein my mind is bewildered upon this very point of renouncing it; for I do not think there is anything in flavor superior to flesh.

sanskrit: tad icchāmi guṇāñ śrotuṃ māṃsasyābhakṣaṇe 'pi vā bhakṣaṇe caiva ye doṣās tāṃś caiva puruṣarṣabha
english: Therefore I wish to hear the virtues that lie in the abstention from flesh, and also the faults there are in eating it, O bull among men.

sanskrit: sarvaṃ tattvena dharmajña yathāvad iha dharmataḥ kiṃ vā bhakṣyam abhakṣyaṃ vā sarvam etad vadasva me
english: Tell me all of this truly and in accordance with dharma, O knower of dharma: what is to be eaten and what is not to be eaten—declare it all to me.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evam etan mahābāho yathā vadasi bhārata na māṃsāt param atrānyad rasato vidyate bhuvi
english: Bhīṣma said: It is even so, O mighty-armed Bhārata, as you say; there is nothing else on earth that surpasses flesh in flavor.

sanskrit: kṣatakṣīṇābhitaptānāṃ grāmyadharmaratāś ca ye adhvanā karśitānāṃ ca na māṃsād vidyate param
english: For those wounded, wasted, and feverish, for those given to the householder's life, and for those worn down by travel, there is nothing better than flesh.

sanskrit: sadyo vardhayati prāṇān puṣṭim agryāṃ dadāti ca na bhakṣo 'bhyadhikaḥ kaś cin māṃsād asti paraṃtapa
english: It at once strengthens the vital breath and gives the highest nourishment; there is no food whatever superior to flesh, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: vivarjane tu bahavo guṇāḥ kauravanandana ye bhavanti manuṣyāṇāṃ tān me nigadataḥ śṛṇu
english: Yet many are the virtues that come to men from abstaining from it, O joy of the Kurus; hear these from me as I tell them.

sanskrit: svamāṃsaṃ paramāṃsair yo vivardhayitum icchati nāsti kṣudrataras tasmān na nṛśaṃsataro naraḥ
english: There is no man meaner, none more cruel, than he who wishes to fatten his own flesh with the flesh of others.

sanskrit: na hi prāṇāt priyataraṃ loke kiṃ cana vidyate tasmād dayāṃ naraḥ kuryād yathātmani tathā pare
english: For in this world nothing is dearer than one's own life; therefore let a man show compassion to others as he would to himself.

sanskrit: śukrāc ca tāta saṃbhūtir māṃsasyeha na saṃśayaḥ bhakṣaṇe tu mahān doṣo vadhena saha kalpate
english: Flesh, my son, arises here from the seed of life—of this there is no doubt; and in eating it there is great fault, joined with killing.

sanskrit: ahiṃsālakṣaṇo dharma iti vedavido viduḥ yad ahiṃsraṃ bhavet karma tat kuryād ātmavān naraḥ
english: Those who know the Veda understand that dharma is marked by non-violence; whatever deed is free of harm, that let the self-possessed man perform.

sanskrit: pitṛdaivatayajñeṣu prokṣitaṃ havir ucyate vidhinā vedadṛṣṭena tad bhuktveha na duṣyati
english: In the sacrifices to the ancestors and the gods, the consecrated oblation is so named according to the ordinance seen in the Veda; having eaten that, one is not defiled.

sanskrit: yajñārthe paśavaḥ sṛṣṭā ity api śrūyate śrutiḥ ato 'nyathā pravṛttānāṃ rākṣaso vidhir ucyate
english: The sacred teaching is also heard that 'animals were created for sacrifice'; for those who act otherwise than this, the rite is called demonic.

sanskrit: kṣatriyāṇāṃ tu yo dṛṣṭo vidhis tam api me śṛṇu vīryeṇopārjitaṃ māṃsaṃ yathā khādan na duṣyati
english: But hear from me also the rule prescribed for the kṣatriyas, how one eating flesh won by valor is not defiled.

sanskrit: āraṇyāḥ sarvadaivatyāḥ prokṣitāḥ sarvaśo mṛgāḥ agastyena purā rājan mṛgayā yena pūjyate
english: The wild deer of the forest were of old consecrated as sacred to all the gods by Agastya, O king, by whom the hunt is thus sanctioned.

sanskrit: nātmānam aparityajya mṛgayā nāma vidyate samatām upasaṃgamya rūpaṃ hanyān na vā nṛpa
english: There is no hunting without staking one's own self; meeting the beast on equal terms, he may slay it or be slain, O king.

sanskrit: ato rājarṣayaḥ sarve mṛgayāṃ yānti bhārata lipyante na hi doṣeṇa na caitat pātakaṃ viduḥ
english: Hence all the royal sages go to the hunt, O Bhārata; they are not stained by fault, nor do they reckon this a sin.

sanskrit: na hi tatparamaṃ kiṃ cid iha loke paratra ca yat sarveṣv iha lokeṣu dayā kauravanandana
english: For there is nothing higher than this, here or hereafter, in all the worlds—nothing higher than compassion, O joy of the Kurus.

sanskrit: na bhayaṃ vidyate jātu narasyeha dayāvataḥ dayāvatām ime lokāḥ pare cāpi tapasvinām
english: No fear ever befalls a compassionate man here; these worlds belong to the compassionate, and the higher worlds belong to ascetics.

sanskrit: abhayaṃ sarvabhūtebhyo yo dadāti dayāparaḥ abhayaṃ tasya bhūtāni dadatīty anuśuśrumaḥ
english: He who, given to compassion, grants freedom from fear to all creatures—to him the creatures in turn grant freedom from fear: so have we heard.

sanskrit: kṣataṃ ca skhalitaṃ caiva patitaṃ kliṣṭam āhatam sarvabhūtāni rakṣanti sameṣu viṣameṣu ca
english: All beings protect him—wounded, stumbling, fallen, afflicted, or struck down—both on even ground and on rough.

sanskrit: nainaṃ vyālamṛgā ghnanti na piśācā na rākṣasāḥ mucyante bhayakāleṣu mokṣayanti ca ye parān
english: Beasts of prey do not slay him, nor piśācas, nor rākṣasas; in times of peril those are set free who set others free.

sanskrit: prāṇadānāt paraṃ dānaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati na hy ātmanaḥ priyataraḥ kaś cid astīti niścitam
english: No gift greater than the gift of life has ever been or shall ever be, for it is certain that nothing is dearer to anyone than one's own self.

sanskrit: aniṣṭaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ maraṇaṃ nāma bhārata mṛtyukāle hi bhūtānāṃ sadyo jāyati vepathuḥ
english: Death, O Bhārata, is unwelcome to all beings; for at the hour of death a trembling arises at once in living things.

sanskrit: jātijanmajarāduḥkhe nityaṃ saṃsārasāgare jantavaḥ parivartante maraṇād udvijanti ca
english: In the ocean of transmigration, with its ceaseless sorrow of birth, caste, and old age, creatures revolve and shrink in dread from death.

sanskrit: garbhavāseṣu pacyante kṣārāmlakaṭukai rasaiḥ mūtraśleṣmapurīṣāṇāṃ sparśaiś ca bhṛśadāruṇaiḥ
english: In their dwellings in the womb they are cooked by the briny, sour, and pungent humors, and by the exceedingly grievous touch of urine, phlegm, and excrement.

sanskrit: jātāś cāpy avaśās tatra bhidyamānāḥ punaḥ punaḥ pāṭyamānāś ca dṛśyante vivaśā māṃsagṛddhinaḥ
english: And even when born, those greedy for flesh are seen there helpless, torn apart again and again, and cut to pieces, powerless.

sanskrit: kumbhīpāke ca pacyante tāṃ tāṃ yonim upāgatāḥ ākramya māryamāṇāś ca bhrāmyante vai punaḥ punaḥ
english: They are boiled in the Kumbhīpāka hell, and entering one womb after another, set upon and slain, they are made to wander again and again.

sanskrit: nātmano 'sti priyataraḥ pṛthivyām anusṛtya ha tasmāt prāṇiṣu sarveṣu dayāvān ātmavān bhavet
english: Considering well, there is on earth none dearer to a being than its own self; therefore let the self-possessed man be compassionate toward all living creatures.

sanskrit: sarvamāṃsāni yo rājan yāvajjīvaṃ na bhakṣayet svarge sa vipulaṃ sthānaṃ prāpnuyān nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: He who, O king, eats no flesh at all so long as he lives shall obtain a vast abode in heaven—of this there is no doubt.
